title: Building pi in a World of Slop — Mario Zechner
talk_summary: Mario Zechner argues that current coding-agent harnesses over-engineer context (system reminders, LSP-error injection, tool-output pruning) and that minimal harnesses like Terminus outperform native ones on Terminal Bench. He then warns that many parallel agents compound unreviewed defects with no learning or bottleneck, and prescribes scoping tasks tightly, modularizing code, capping generated code under review, and hand-writing critical code.

takeaways.technique: Minimal system prompt and tool set
takeaways.what_they_do: Ships a tiny system prompt and only four tools (read, write, edit, bash) because models are post-trained as coding agents and don't need long instructions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You don't need 10,000 tokens to tell them, "You're a coding agent." They know, because they are coding agents now.

takeaways.what_they_do: Criticizes harnesses that query an LSP after every edit and inject errors into the tool result, arguing it breaks the model's flow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You're not writing a line of code, checking the errors, writing the next line, checking the errors.

takeaways.technique: Cap generated code under review; hand-write critical paths
takeaways.what_they_do: Limits how much agent-generated code a human must review and insists critical code be read line-by-line or written by hand.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Cap the amount of generated code uh that you need to review. And non-critical code, sure, five slope ahead. Critical code, read every line.

takeaways.what_they_do: Argues parallel agents compound errors with no learning or bottleneck, and that tasks must be scoped so the agent can find everything it needs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you can scope it in such a way that the agent is guaranteed to find all the things it needs to find to do a good job, you're done.

takeaways.technique: Don't trust agent-written tests or review agents alone
takeaways.what_they_do: Warns that review agents ('the ouroboros') catch only some issues and that agent-written tests can't be trusted as a safety net.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Then you say, "Oh, I have a review agent." Let me introduce you to the wonderful world of the ouroboros. Doesn't work.

takeaways.technique: Route only well-suited tasks to agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Lists good agent tasks: scoped work, tasks with an evaluator for hill-climbing, non-mission-critical/boring work, and reproducing user issues from partial info.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Reproduction cases for user issues, which are usually only partial in information, perfect.
